subject: test-planner
reason: Five e2e cases: the remove button's accessible name for the story's product, unchanged visible text, unchanged remove behaviour, per-line product interpolation with two products, and removal limited to the named line; this round only fixed MD033 inline-HTML placeholders.

excluded.item: Accessible names of the header bag button, page heading and footer
excluded.reason: Already say 'shopping bag' per the bug report; the story changes only the remove button
The accessible name is rendered markup that only the WebApp on the test stack shows, so the cases run e2e

items.title: Remove button is named "Remove Wanderer Black Hiking Boots from your shopping bag"
covers: Expected: accessible name 'Remove Wanderer Black Hiking Boots from your shopping bag'
items.reason: This is the bug's acceptance criterion verbatim: repeating the reproduction steps must yield the accessible name "Remove Wanderer Black Hiking Boots from your shopping bag" instead of "… from your bag". The name is set in Razor markup and computed by the browser's accessibility tree, so only an e2e test through the WebApp observes it; it also asserts the old name is gone so a regression back to "bag" fails.

items.title: Remove button's visible text is still "Remove"
items.reason: The story explicitly requires the button's visible text to stay "Remove"; a fix that changes the visible label (or puts the long accessible name on screen) would break the line's layout and violate the contract. Visible text is only observable in the rendered page, so this runs e2e, separately from the accessible-name case because it checks a different property.

items.title: Activating the remove button still removes the line from the shopping bag
covers: Expected: what the remove button does is unchanged
items.reason: The story requires the button's behaviour to be unchanged: it submits the line's form with quantity 0 and the line disappears. Editing the button's markup risks breaking its `name`/`value` submit pair; the effect spans the WebApp form handler and the Basket service, so it is checked end to end through the UI.

items.title: Each line's remove button names its own product with "from your shopping bag"
covers: Bug Report: each line's remove button is named 'Remove {product} from your shopping bag'
items.reason: The bug report says each line's remove button carries the name `Remove {product} from your …`; the fix must keep the product interpolation per line while changing the trailing wording. A hard-coded name for one product would pass TC-PRB-6-01 but fail here, so a second product is needed. Runs e2e for the same reason as TC-PRB-6-01.

items.title: The remove button named for one product does not remove the other line
covers: Expected: what the remove button does is unchanged
Bug Report: each line's remove button names its own product
items.reason: The accessible name promises `Remove {product} from your shopping bag`, so the button must act only on the line whose product it names; a fix that rewires the button's form or `name`/`value` pair could remove the wrong line or every line while the single-line case TC-PRB-6-03 still passes. This is the boundary between two adjacent lines, which only the rendered page and the Basket service together can show, so it runs e2e.
